objective: A person can install project protection, set up a new or existing Linux Python, Node.js or TypeScript project in 60 seconds or less on the declared supported developer-machine profile, then work normally in protected Codex. Shared project/task scope, package controls and escalation must remain active. Do not replace first setup with warm reopening.
completion_rule: All mandatory requirements need fresh behavioral evidence against the final runtime. Passing old tests, completing a queue or a model saying done is insufficient. Missing evidence is incomplete. Scope reductions require operator approval; no silent waivers.

scope.platform: Ordinary x86_64 Linux developer machine with supported kernel, systemd user session and package ecosystem runtime. Measure clean application installation; record every OS prerequisite. No test on the operator laptop.
scope.agents: Codex CLI first, multiple independent parents and registered narrower delegates. Other clients are not claimed supported without a separately tested adapter.
scope.external_boundaries: Browser login/MFA requires the owner. Never copy authentication. Report full elapsed time and machine-controlled elapsed time separately. Do not call a cached or already-approved run a first setup.

requirements.text: One advertised installation entry point without cloning benchmark history or manual PATH plumbing; preflight, repeat invocation, upgrade/rollback and safe uninstall; preserve unrelated files and project data.

Measure from first installer invocation through fresh project scope review and protected Codex readiness, plus first successful protected operation. Absolute maximum <=60s on declared developer-machine profile; aim for about 40s; separate human, authentication, downloads and caches honestly. No deferred unchecked package execution.

New and existing project autodetection; concise human-readable scope/package/escalation proposal and explicit approval. Existing activity is not automatic authority. Rejected/cancelled/failed setup must not corrupt the project.

Six fresh/existing Python/Node/TypeScript terminal journeys and a mixed repo. Safe supported runtime selection, common lockfiles/workspaces and local dependencies; clear safe handling of unavailable toolchains/private credentials.
Real edit/build/test, controlled localhost development service, safe local Git operations, reviewed dependency changes, and protected conversation resume while retaining policy and violations.

Approved direct/transitive package identities, critical CVSS rejection, configurable minimum age, artifact integrity, isolated builds, no unchecked dependency execution. Policy-aware resolution must allow valid older releases when permitted rather than selecting a rejected newest release and calling that success.
Recheck installed environments against fresh advisory evidence, quarantine confirmed newly forbidden dependencies, fail safely on uncertain evidence, do not classify outages as agent misconduct.
Non-bypassable local tool boundary; all parents/delegates under same project; tasks only narrow; ordinary model refusal is not proof of controls.
Shared warnings and thresholds stop registered running work and reject later launches; unrelated work continues. Failure/restart/revision do not silently reset stop history.

Fresh installation following only documentation; useful positive work and negative probes; all mandatory Linux tests with no hidden skips; independent post-implementation review. Evidence includes source hashes, effects and timings.
Minimal dependencies, reproducible user docs, sanitized artifacts, credential review, progressive commits and verified public push. Existing paper and frozen evidence unchanged.

known_at_start: 0.5 tests pass but first-time setup is not certified <=30s.
Common workspace/local/private/mixed layouts need explicit support.
Package checks are installation-time, not ongoing.
Installer needs clone/manual PATH and prerequisites.
First new-account OAuth ceremony was not tested.
